The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Moon in the Mixing Bowl

At dusk, Bella took a mixing bowl outside. Tomorrow it could hold snacks for Everybody Day. Tonight it held a puddle from the rain and, right in the puddle, a little round moon.

Moth flew down beside her. “My cousins will come in the evening,” she said. “How will they find the gate?” Bella looked at the moon in the bowl. “I shall lend them this lamp.”

She pushed the bowl to the gate. The water sloshed. The moon fell right out. Bella looked behind the bowl. She looked under the dock. She looked accusingly at one particularly shiny snail.

“Stand where I’m standing,” Moth called from a post. Bella flew up beside her. There was the moon in the water again. When she moved her head, the little moon moved too.

“Well,” said Bella, “that is a lamp with very particular ideas.” From the post she could see something else. Two tall stems bent toward each other above the gate. Together they looked like an enormous pair of whiskers.

Moth flew a circle. “I see the whiskers!” she called from the bean rows. She saw them from the hedge, too. Even when a cloud covered the moon, the stems stood tall against the last pale sky.

Bella drew the bowl between the two stems on a Welcome Tree leaf. “Will you try the whiskers before the big day?” she asked Moth’s cousins. That evening each found the gate. Each found something nice waiting in the bowl.

After the moths went home, Bella rinsed the bowl and set it on the step. She found one last visitor floating in the water. “You may stay till breakfast,” she told the moon.

What shape could you recognize after sunset?
